explanations.answer: He invites a little child to stand among them
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. The disciples ask a big question and Jesus doesn't give them a speech first. He invites a little child to stand among them (Matthew 18:2). Sometimes the best answer is just standing there in the middle of the room.

explanations.answer: He sends them up the mountain to pray
explanations.explanation: No mountain trip here, friend. The text says Jesus invited a little child to stand among them (Matthew 18:2). The answer was already in the room, and nobody had to hike for it.

explanations.answer: He writes in the dirt with His finger
explanations.explanation: That's a different moment, baker. Here, Jesus doesn't write anything. He invites a little child to stand among the disciples (Matthew 18:2). The whole lesson is standing right there on two small feet.

explanations.answer: You will never enter the kingdom of heaven
explanations.explanation: Right, baker. Jesus says, "Truly I tell you, unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven." (Matthew 18:3). He starts with "Truly I tell you," so you know He means it. The change He talks about is becoming like little children.

explanations.answer: You will be the least among your brothers
explanations.explanation: Close in feel, friend, but that's not what He says. Jesus says that without that change and becoming like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven (Matthew 18:3). That's about getting in, not about where you rank once you're inside.

explanations.answer: You will lose the reward you have earned
explanations.explanation: I get why that sounds right, baker. But Jesus doesn't mention a reward here. He says unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven (Matthew 18:3). The change comes first, before anything else.

explanations.answer: Whoever humbles himself like this little child
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. Jesus says, "Therefore, whoever humbles himself like this little child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven." (Matthew 18:4). The disciples asked who ranks highest, and Jesus pointed at a child. I'm still waiting on a trophy for MY humility, which tells you how I'm doing.

explanations.answer: Whoever gives the most away to the poor
explanations.explanation: Giving is good, friend, but that's not the answer here. Jesus says the greatest is whoever humbles himself like this little child (Matthew 18:4). He's talking about humility, not a total.

explanations.answer: Whoever has followed Him the longest
explanations.explanation: Nice try, baker. The disciples had been with Jesus a good while, but He doesn't give the title to the longest follower. He says whoever humbles himself like this little child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven (Matthew 18:4). Time on the counter doesn't count here.

explanations.answer: True
explanations.explanation: True, baker. Jesus says, "And whoever welcomes a little child like this in My name welcomes Me." (Matthew 18:5). Think about that one. A simple welcome in His name, and Jesus says it's welcoming Him.

explanations.answer: False
explanations.explanation: It's actually true, friend. The text says, "And whoever welcomes a little child like this in My name welcomes Me." (Matthew 18:5). Jesus says that welcoming a little child in His name is welcoming Him.

explanations.answer: The man through whom they come
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. Jesus says, "These stumbling blocks must come, but woe to the man through whom they come!" (Matthew 18:7). It's a serious line, and I think it shows how much Jesus cares about those little ones.

explanations.answer: The one who trips over them
explanations.explanation: Not quite, friend. The woe isn't for the one who trips. Jesus says, "…woe to the man through whom they come!" (Matthew 18:7). It's aimed at the one who brings the stumbling block.

explanations.answer: The ones who never warned others
explanations.explanation: That's not in the text, baker. Jesus says the stumbling blocks must come, "but woe to the man through whom they come!" (Matthew 18:7). Warning isn't mentioned in this verse at all.

explanations.answer: True
explanations.explanation: Flip that one around, friend. Jesus says it's better to enter life crippled or lame than to have two hands and two feet and be thrown into the eternal fire (Matthew 18:8). Keeping everything and ending up in the fire is the worse deal. Jesus is making a big point about how serious sin is.

explanations.answer: False
explanations.explanation: Right, baker. Jesus says, "It is better for you to enter life crippled or lame than to have two hands and two feet and be thrown into the eternal fire." (Matthew 18:8). Entering life is the better thing, even if it costs you. It's a heavy teaching, and Jesus says it plainly.

explanations.answer: Their angels in heaven always see His Father's face
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. Jesus says, "For I tell you that their angels in heaven always see the face of My Father in heaven." (Matthew 18:10). So these little ones are not small in heaven. Looking down on them is looking down on someone heaven pays attention to.

explanations.answer: They will inherit the whole earth one day
explanations.explanation: That's a good line, friend, but it's from a different place. Here, Jesus' reason is that their angels in heaven always see the face of His Father in heaven (Matthew 18:10). Inheriting the earth isn't mentioned in this passage.

explanations.answer: Their names are written in the book of life
explanations.explanation: I see why that came to mind, baker. But Jesus doesn't mention a book of life here. His reason is that their angels in heaven always see the face of His Father in heaven (Matthew 18:10).

explanations.answer: Leave the ninety-nine and search for the lost one
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. Jesus asks, "will he not leave the ninety-nine on the hills and go out to search for the one that is lost?" (Matthew 18:12). He asks it as a question because He expects everyone to nod. One sheep is missing, and the shepherd goes after it.

explanations.answer: Stay with the ninety-nine and wait for it to return
explanations.explanation: That sounds sensible, friend, but it's not what Jesus says. He says the man will leave the ninety-nine on the hills and go out to search for the one that is lost (Matthew 18:12). Waiting around isn't in the story.

explanations.answer: Send his servants out to bring it home
explanations.explanation: Good guess, baker, but no servants show up. Jesus says the man himself will "go out to search for the one that is lost" (Matthew 18:12). He goes himself.

explanations.answer: True
explanations.explanation: Look closer, baker. Jesus says the man "rejoices more over that one sheep than over the ninety-nine that did not go astray." (Matthew 18:13). It's more, not the same. Finding the lost one brings extra joy.

explanations.answer: False
explanations.explanation: Right, friend. Jesus says, "he rejoices more over that one sheep than over the ninety-nine that did not go astray." (Matthew 18:13). More joy over the one that was found. The ninety-nine aren't forgotten, but the found one gets a big celebration.

explanations.answer: He is not willing that any little one should perish
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. Jesus says, "In the same way, your Father in heaven is not willing that any of these little ones should perish." (Matthew 18:14). The shepherd's search is the picture, and the Father's heart is the point.

explanations.answer: He keeps only the ones who never wander off
explanations.explanation: Not a chance, friend. Jesus tells a story about a sheep that goes astray and gets searched for (Matthew 18:12). Then He says the Father is not willing that any of these little ones should perish (Matthew 18:14).

explanations.answer: He waits for the lost to find their own way back
explanations.explanation: I can see why you picked it, baker. But in Jesus' story, the man goes out to search for the one that is lost (Matthew 18:12). He doesn't wait for it, and Jesus ties that to the Father, who is not willing that any of these little ones should perish (Matthew 18:14).

explanations.answer: You have won your brother over
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. Jesus says, "If he listens to you, you have won your brother over." (Matthew 18:15). Notice the word is "won over," not "won." Getting your brother back is the prize.

explanations.answer: You have proved that you were right
explanations.explanation: Nope, friend, and I think that's the whole point. Jesus says, "If he listens to you, you have won your brother over." (Matthew 18:15). He talks about gaining your brother, not about being right.

explanations.answer: You have done what the Law requires
explanations.explanation: Good thinking, baker, but that's not the phrase here. Jesus says, "If he listens to you, you have won your brother over." (Matthew 18:15). The Law isn't mentioned in that verse.

explanations.answer: Take one or two others along
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. Jesus says, "But if he will not listen, take one or two others along" (Matthew 18:16). The talk stays small. One or two others join you, and that's the next step.

explanations.answer: Let it drop and move on
explanations.explanation: That's not what Jesus says, friend. When your brother won't listen, He says to "take one or two others along" (Matthew 18:16). There's a next step before anyone walks away.

explanations.answer: Write it down and wait
explanations.explanation: I like the neat paperwork, baker, but it's not in the text. Jesus says, "take one or two others along" (Matthew 18:16). It's a person-to-person step, not a note-to-self step.

explanations.answer: witnesses
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. The words are "every matter may be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses." (Matthew 18:16). Jesus is quoting Deuteronomy 19:15. So the one or two others you bring can speak up about what happened.

explanations.answer: elders
explanations.explanation: Close, friend, but not this one. The verse says "two or three witnesses" (Matthew 18:16). Jesus is quoting Deuteronomy 19:15, and the word is witnesses.

explanations.answer: priests
explanations.explanation: No priests in this verse, baker. Jesus says "every matter may be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses." (Matthew 18:16). He's quoting Deuteronomy 19:15, and the word is witnesses.

explanations.answer: The church
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. Jesus says, "If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the church." (Matthew 18:17). It goes from private, to one or two others, to the church. Each step gets a little wider.

explanations.answer: The priests
explanations.explanation: Not quite, friend. After the one or two others, Jesus says, "tell it to the church." (Matthew 18:17). Priests aren't named in this step.

explanations.answer: The town judges
explanations.explanation: I can see how a courtroom comes to mind, baker. But Jesus says, "tell it to the church." (Matthew 18:17). He doesn't mention town judges at all.

explanations.answer: True
explanations.explanation: True, baker. Jesus says, "And if he refuses to listen even to the church, regard him as you would a pagan or a tax collector." (Matthew 18:17). That's the last step in the list. It comes only after the private talk, the one or two others and the church.

explanations.answer: False
explanations.explanation: It's true, friend. The text says, "And if he refuses to listen even to the church, regard him as you would a pagan or a tax collector." (Matthew 18:17). That's the final step Jesus names.

explanations.answer: His Father in heaven
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. Jesus says, "if two of you on the earth agree about anything you ask for, it will be done for you by My Father in heaven." (Matthew 18:19). The answer comes from the Father. Two of you ask, and He does it.

explanations.answer: The angels in heaven
explanations.explanation: Angels do show up earlier in this passage, friend, but not here. Jesus says it "will be done for you by My Father in heaven." (Matthew 18:19). The Father is the one who does it.

explanations.answer: The elders of the church
explanations.explanation: Good guess, baker, since the church came up in the last step. But Jesus says it will be done "by My Father in heaven." (Matthew 18:19). No elders are named in this verse.

explanations.answer: Jesus Himself
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. Jesus says, "For where two or three gather together in My name, there am I with them." (Matthew 18:20). "There am I" means Jesus is speaking about Himself. Two or three people gathered in His name, and He's with them.

explanations.answer: an angel
explanations.explanation: Not an angel, friend. Jesus says, "there am I with them." (Matthew 18:20). He's talking about Himself being there.

explanations.answer: a prophet
explanations.explanation: No prophet in this verse, baker. Jesus says, "For where two or three gather together in My name, there am I with them." (Matthew 18:20). The one who is there is Jesus Himself.
